_comment: Facts live here, not in the model. Everything under 'specs', 'verdict_facts' and 'image' is copied verbatim into the page. Gemini only writes prose around them.
_verify_before_running: SanDisk Extreme SSD V2: official data sheet gives read speed (2000 MB/s) but not an exact write speed - only that it's lower. Confirm a real write-speed figure from a second source (retailer listing or independent test) before publishing, or leave the spec table as-is (it already omits an invented number).
Insta360 Flow 2 Pro: max phone/payload weight was not published on any official page checked - not included below. Add it only once you've confirmed it from the manual or Insta360 support.
Insta360 Flow 2 Pro: whether the AI Tracker hardware is bundled or sold separately varies by current promo/SKU - re-check store.insta360.com before publishing the con line about it.
DJI Mic Mini: showed as out of stock on DJI's own store at research time - confirm current availability via B&H/Amazon before adding an ASIN.
Ulanzi VL49 Pro: the 90-minute runtime figure is Ulanzi's own claim, no independent test found to cross-check.
No product below has an image yet - image.src points to a filename under images/ that you still need to add at the width/height listed.
No ASIN is set for any product - each page will render the site's 'link pending' placeholder until you add one.

Prices are deliberately left out of every spec table - the site's compliance rule bans live price figures in the UI (see references/compliance.md); the build script's own check() function will hold any page that slips one in.

products.name: DJI Mic Mini
products.audience: solo creators and vloggers who want a barely-there wireless mic without extra features they won't use

image.alt: DJI Mic Mini wireless transmitter clipped to a shirt collar

known_pros: Transmitter weighs about 10 g, so it barely shows clipped to a shirt or jacket
400 m open-field range covers far more distance than most vlogging or interview setups need
Charging case adds days of use in the field without a laptop nearby
known_cons: DJI's spec page doesn't list on-device recording storage, so confirm that separately if you need backup audio
Two radios (2.4 GHz plus Bluetooth) means more that can go wrong to troubleshoot than a simple wired lav

Range and battery in real use

products.name: Ulanzi VL49 Pro
products.audience: mobile creators who need a pocketable fill or key light for short clips, interviews or product shots where colour accuracy matters

image.alt: Ulanzi VL49 Pro mini RGB light mounted on a cold shoe

known_pros: CRI of 95 or higher is a real step up for accurate skin tones at this price
Magnetic mount plus built-in RGB effects add flexibility for creative shots
USB-C charging matches modern phones, no separate proprietary cable to carry
known_cons: About 90 minutes at high brightness is short for a long shoot, and that figure is Ulanzi's own claim rather than an independent test
No IP or weather rating is listed, so treat it as indoor or handheld use only
faq_questions: Is the Ulanzi VL49 Pro bright enough for outdoor filming?
Can the VL49 Pro mount directly to a phone cage?

products.name: SanDisk Extreme Portable SSD (V2)
products.audience: creators offloading raw 4K or ProRes footage in the field who need rugged, pocket-sized storage

image.alt: SanDisk Extreme Portable SSD V2 next to a smartphone for scale

known_pros: IP65 dust and water resistance plus a 3 m drop rating suit outdoor, run-and-gun shooting
46.9 g and pocket-sized, easy to carry as a backup drive
20 Gbps interface leaves headroom for high-bitrate 4K or ProRes if your adapter supports it
known_cons: SanDisk's own data sheet doesn't publish an exact write speed, only that it's lower than the 2,000 MB/s read figure, so treat write performance as unconfirmed until tested
Hitting the rated speed needs a USB 3.2 Gen 2×2 port and cable, which most phones and older laptops don't have
faq_questions: Will the SanDisk Extreme SSD work directly with an iPhone?
Is 2,000 MB/s realistic for editing ProRes footage?

products.name: SmallRig Universal Mobile Phone Cage (2791B)
products.source: SmallRig's product listing on B&H Photo
products.audience: creators building a modular rig around a phone who want more mounting points than a minimalist cage offers

image.alt: SmallRig Universal Mobile Phone Cage holding a smartphone with cold shoe mounts visible

known_pros: Four cold shoe mounts is generous for stacking a mic, light and monitor at once
Screw-tightened clamp holds securely across a wide range of phone widths
Aluminum construction adds rigidity over plastic cages at a similar price
known_cons: No 3/8" threads are listed, which can limit compatibility with some tripod heads without an adapter
Screw-tightening is slower to mount and remove than a spring-loaded cage, which matters for fast run-and-gun shooting
faq_questions: Does the SmallRig 2791B fit phones with thick cases?
How many accessories can you mount at once?

products.name: Insta360 Flow 2 Pro
products.audience: iPhone-centric solo creators who want automated subject tracking without holding the phone themselves

image.alt: Insta360 Flow 2 Pro gimbal folded next to its magnetic phone clamp

known_pros: Apple DockKit support brings AI tracking to 200+ iOS apps without opening Insta360's own app
10-hour battery life is long for a folding gimbal
Fast charging reaches 80% in under an hour for quick turnarounds between shoots
known_cons: The AI Tracker hardware needed for full subject tracking is sold separately on some Flow 2 Pro bundles, so check what's included before buying
faq_questions: Does the Insta360 Flow 2 Pro work with Android phones?
